# @zakkster/lite-gpu-profiler

> Zero-GC WebGL2 render-path telemetry. Passive INSTRUMENT (measures work), the
> counterpart to @zakkster/lite-vram's active MANAGER (manages texture memory). Two
> telemetry kinds with two homes: deterministic command COUNTERS (draw calls,
> instances, floats uploaded) recorded in a GL-agnostic headless core, and async GPU
> TIME from an EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 pool (browser only). Counters gate
> EXACTLY and headlessly in the same matrix as lite-profiler; GPU time gates by
> tolerance. ESM only, MIT.

## Why two homes

- Command counts are integers the caller already has at flush time -- they need no
  GL. Recorded in the GL-agnostic core, they are deterministic (identical on every
  host/run) and gate with zero tolerance and no GPU, in CI, today.
- GPU time is a live-context measurement and is noisy. It comes from GpuTimerPool
  (browser), resolved asynchronously, and gates by fractional tolerance.

This mirrors lite-gl's own split: counters extend the headless tested core; the
timer extends the browser smoke test.

## Exports

- `GpuProfiler` (main, headless): the counter + GPU-time aggregator.
- `GpuTimerPool` (subpath `@zakkster/lite-gpu-profiler/timer`, browser): the async
  timer-query pool.
- `checkGpuRegression` / `assertNoGpuRegression` / `GPU_DEFAULT_RULES`: the gate.

## GpuProfiler (headless core)

    new GpuProfiler(capacity?, { counters? })   // counters default [drawCalls, instances, floatsUploaded]
    beginFrame()                                 // clear per-frame accumulators (call every frame)
    recordDraw(instanceCount?)                   // drawCalls += 1; instances += n   (only when a draw happens)
    recordUpload(floatCount)                     // floatsUploaded += n               (the dirty-range signal)
    add(tag, n?)                                 // arbitrary tracked counter
    recordGpuTime(ms)                            // ingest a resolved GPU-time sample from the pool
    endFrame()                                   // flush frame totals to rings
    summary(meta?)                               // { counters:{tag:{sum,min,max,avg,last}}, framesDrawn,
                                                 //   framesSkipped, gpu:{avg,min,max,p01,p99,samples}, ... }
    reset() / destroy()

Hot path (record*) allocates nothing: it writes a Float64 accumulator or pushes one
float to a lite-ring-buffer ring. Counter rings are Float32-backed, so per-frame
counter VALUES are exact up to 2^24 (16,777,216) -- e.g. 2M instances x 8 floats.
Beyond that they quantize deterministically (identical runs still gate equal, but
printed values round). `framesDrawn`/`framesSkipped` are derived from the
drawCalls ring (a frame that skipped its draw recorded no drawCalls), so the
"redraw-only-on-change" claim is verifiable without an extra counter.

## GpuTimerPool (browser)

    new GpuTimerPool(gl, { poolSize?, onSample? })   // poolSize bounds in-flight queries (default 8)
    begin()   // resolve every consecutively-finished query, then open a new one (call before the draw)
    end()     // end the open query (call after the draw)
    onSample(cb) / dispose()

WebGL2 timer queries are asynchronous: a result lands 1-3 frames after end(). The
pool keeps a fixed ring of pre-allocated query objects, starts AT MOST one region
per frame (only one TIME_ELAPSED query may be active at a time -- no nesting),
drains every consecutively-finished query on each begin(), reads results late, and
DROPS a frame whose GPU_DISJOINT flag is set (context switch/throttle make the
timing meaningless). When the GPU runs more than poolSize frames behind, the pool
skips opening new regions until pending ones ripen: sustained result latency of L
frames thins sampling to ~poolSize/L of frames -- it never drops a pending query,
which would starve sampling entirely. It never allocates after construction and
deletes every query on dispose (no leaked handles). If the extension is missing,
`supported` is false and begin/end are no-ops.

## Wiring into @zakkster/lite-gl

lite-gl draws the whole instanced field in one call per frame, so the sink's draw()
IS the frame boundary. Two seams:

- COUNTERS in the GL-agnostic core (headless, matrix-gated). Where GLBackend's sink
  is called from `reactiveField.flush`, forward the arguments:
      upload(data, floatOffset, floatCount, instanceOffset, stride) -> profiler.recordUpload(floatCount)
      draw(count)                                                   -> profiler.recordDraw(count)
  and bracket the frame with profiler.beginFrame()/endFrame(). floatsUploaded then
  verifies dirty-range batching: a one-instance change uploads one stride, never the
  whole buffer.
- GPU TIME in the WebGL2 sink (browser). In createPointSink, build a
  GpuTimerPool(gl, { onSample: (ms) => profiler.recordGpuTime(ms) }); call
  pool.begin() before gl.drawArrays and pool.end() after. Recreate the pool in
  onContextRestored (queries die with the context).

## Gate

    checkGpuRegression(baseline, candidate, rules?) -> { ok, verdict, regressions, inconclusive, warnings }
    assertNoGpuRegression(baseline, candidate, rules?)   // throws; err.report carries the result

The gate is fail-closed and tri-state. verdict is 'pass' | 'fail' | 'inconclusive';
ok === (verdict === 'pass'). A rule it cannot evaluate against real measurements --
a gpu.* stat with gpu.samples === 0 (headless CI, no timer extension), a poisoned
non-finite/null stat, or a counter tag tracked by neither summary -- routes to
inconclusive, never a green pass. Two summaries whose `schema` tokens differ are
incomparable and short-circuit to inconclusive before any rule runs (undefined vs
undefined is NOT a mismatch: two hand-rolled summaries from the same producer).
assertNoGpuRegression throws GpuRegressionError on 'fail' and GpuInconclusiveError on
'inconclusive' (both carry .report). A misspelled rule path throws GpuRuleError
("valid paths are ...") before any evaluation.

The report also carries a `warnings` array (always present, never affects
verdict/ok): an `exact` rule whose operands reach 2^24 is flagged, because the
Float32 counter ring quantizes there and a sub-quantum regression is invisible.

The error classes are NOT exported from the package entry point, so CI branches on
`err.name === 'GpuRegressionError'` / `'GpuInconclusiveError'` and on
`err.report.verdict`, not on `instanceof`.

Rule kinds per metric path (`counter.<tag>.<sum|max|min|avg|last>` or `gpu.<field>`):
  { exact: true }      -> regress if candidate != baseline   (deterministic counters)
  { max: N }           -> regress if candidate > N           (absolute ceiling)
  { tolerance: 0.15 }  -> regress if (cand-base)/base > 0.15  (noisy GPU time)

Defaults gate the two claims that matter: counter.floatsUploaded.max (dirty-range)
and counter.drawCalls.max (draw-call count) exactly, gpu.p99 within 15%.

## Coverage

- Core counters + gate: node:test, headless, deterministic (see test/).
- Timer-pool state machine (cycling, lag, FIFO order, disjoint-drop, pool reuse =
  zero per-frame alloc, no leaked handles): node:test against a mock gl.
- Actual GPU nanoseconds: driver-reported via TIME_ELAPSED_EXT and NOT verified in
  this package (no WebGL2 under node). What is verified is the state machine and the
  ns->ms conversion, against a mock gl.

## Scope (v1)

- v1 is frame-level (one GPU-time region per frame), which matches lite-gl's single
  instanced draw. Per-pass timing (sequential queries) and pass-scoped counters are
  deferred. An optional dev-only gl-context monkey-patcher for automatic command
  counting during discovery is a separate supplemental tool; production gates run on
  the explicit API.
